Asha — thanks, happy to break this down. Attached is a draft SOW and a pricing workbook that walks through three packaging options (node-licensed, seat-based, blended metered). High level answers below and I can schedule a short sync with procurement if useful.

Platform fee amortization
- We typically present the platform fee as an annualized subscription line on the invoice, but for accounting-friendly terms we can amortize it monthly across the committed term.
- Example in the workbook: $180k platform fee -> option to recognize as $15k/month over 12 months or as a 12-month prepaid invoice with pro-rated credits on early termination.

Support tiers
- Standard: 9x5 email + ticket SLA, includes up to 10 engineering support hours/month for operational onboarding tasks.
- Premium: 24x7 pager, 4h critical response SLA, includes a 0.5 FTE retainer (40 hours/mo) for runbook adjustments and quarterly architecture reviews.
- Optional: Onsite/remote migration days (billed as pre-agreed FTE days); we can include a migration retainer in the quote.

Exit & decommissioning
- We offer an exit assistance package: data export, ops runbook transfer, and one 4-week run of dual-run for verification.
- We can cap egress costs for the first 30 days post-termination at a negotiated amount if Cordura would like predictability.

Next steps:
- Marissa, Vanessa — can you review the SOW and confirm which support tier and amortization approach we can offer as standard for this enterprise pilot?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks

Looping Markus for legal/pricing guardrails. My quick take:
- Amortization: we can offer monthly amortization for pilot (<=12 months) with a 30% early-exit recapture for platform fee if Cordura terminates before month 9. That mirrors other pilots and keeps revenue recognition clean.
- Support: propose Premium for 6 months of pilot at a 20% discounted retainer, then true-up at renewal. That gives Cordura confidence during onboarding.
- Egress cap: acceptable to commit to a $15k capped egress window for 30 days. Anything beyond is charged at standard rate with prior notice.

Markus — any hard blockers from legal on the 30% early exit recapture or the fixed egress cap?

—Marissa

Marissa — thanks. Legal tweak suggestions:
1) Early-exit recapture: prefer sliding scale (50% recapture if exit <= 3 months, 30% for 4-6 months, 10% for 7-9 months, 0% thereafter). This protects the company given engineering ramp.
2) Egress cap: fine with $15k, but add an exception carve-out for cross-region transfer costs and third-party storage egress (we can name exceptions).
3) Support credits: ensure we include a clause that unused retainer hours do not carry beyond the billing quarter but can be purchased at a discounted uplift.

I'll draft the clause language and push to the Drive folder.

-Markus

Asha — thanks for the patience. We've incorporated internal feedback and attached a redline-friendly SOW and a one-page commercial summary showing three alternatives:

A) Pilot (6 months): monthly amortized platform fee, Premium support at 20% pilot discount, 30% exit recapture if terminated before month 9, $15k egress cap (exceptions called out).
B) 12-month committed on-prem: blended node + metered consumption, platform fee amortized monthly, Premium included for first 3 months then Standard thereafter unless upgraded.
C) Enterprise (36 months): discounted platform fee, flexible credit for migration, negotiated on-call retainer and SLOs.

Would Cordura prefer we present A as a straight pilot PO (fast start) or B with a 12-month commitment that gives lower effective $/token? Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk procurement through the one-pager.
